title: Rigveda 8.57: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.57: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.57 is a hymn of 4 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 628v-629r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.57.1-4 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 4, varga 28); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 629r
translation.original_text:
1yu̱vaṁ de̍vā̱ kratu̍nā pū̱rvyeṇa̍ yu̱ktā rathe̍na tavi̱ṣaṁ ya̍jatrā | āga̍cchataṁ nāsatyā̱ śacī̍bhir i̱daṁ tṛ̱tīya̱ṁ sava̍nam pibāthaḥ ||
2yu̱vāṁ de̱vās traya̍ ekāda̱śāsa̍ḥ sa̱tyāḥ sa̱tyasya̍ dadṛśe pu̱rastā̍t | a̱smāka̍ṁ ya̱jñaṁ sava̍naṁ juṣā̱ṇā pā̱taṁ soma̍m aśvinā̱ dīdya̍gnī ||
3pa̱nāyya̱ṁ tad a̍śvinā kṛ̱taṁ vā̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bho di̱vo raja̍saḥ pṛthi̱vyāḥ | sa̱hasra̱ṁ śaṁsā̍ u̱ta ye gavi̍ṣṭau̱ sarvā̱m̐ it tām̐ upa̍ yātā̱ piba̍dhyai ||
4a̱yaṁ vā̍m bhā̱go nihi̍to yajatre̱mā giro̍ nāsa̱tyopa̍ yātam | piba̍ta̱ṁ soma̱m madhu̍mantam a̱sme pra dā̱śvāṁsa̍m avata̱ṁ śacī̍bhiḥ ||
translation.text:
1ENDOWED, O Gods, with your primeval wisdom, come quickly with your chariot, O ye Holy. Come with your mighty powers, O ye Nâsatyas; come hither, drink ye this the third libation.
2The truthful Deities, the Three-and-Thirty, saw you approach before the Ever-Truthful. Accepting this our worship and libation, O Aṣvins bright with fire, drink ye the Soma.
3Aṣvins, that work of yours deserves our wonder,– the Bull of heaven and earth and air's mid region; Yea, and your thousand promises in battle, -to all of these come near and drink beside us.
4Here is your portion laid for you, ye Holy: come to these songs of ours, O ye Nâsatyas. Drink among us the Soma full of sweetness, and with your powers assist the man who worships.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 629r (numbered 51r by the scribe) (OPenn image 629, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 8.57.1 ‹-yajatrā ā agacchatam nāsatyā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 629v (numbered 51v by the scribe), begins in RV 8.58.3 ‹-jyotiṣmantam ketu-mantam tri-cakram su-kham›. Verses 8.57.1-4 end on this page; 8.57.1 begins on fol. 628v (numbered 50v by the scribe).
